content.text:
I've read the release and the brief line by line. Here is my check.

**Notable finding:** the Investment Management prior-year comparison in the brief ("$1.5 billion a year ago") does not round correctly — the release shows $1,552 million for 2Q 2025, which rounds to $1.6 billion. Also worth flagging for the committee: several bundled facts are only half-covered — the brief gives Wealth Management net revenues but never the 30.5% pre-tax margin, gives the $148 billion net new assets figure but omits that just over half came from Workplace-channel IPO inflows (a one-off composition point), gives Equity revenues without the +69% growth, and gives CET1 without the 15.0% prior-year comparison.

facts.evidence: Morgan Stanley reports record second quarter 2026 net revenues of $21.3 billion and EPS of $3.46. ... The Firm reported net revenues of $21.3 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with $16.8 billion for the same period a year ago.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion, or $3.46 per diluted share, compared with $3.5 billion, or $2.13 per diluted share, for the same period a year ago.

**Institutional Securities:** Reported net revenues of $11.0 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with $7.6 billion a year ago. (the 'record' label is omitted, but figures, period and basis are right)
The Firm reported a return on average tangible common equity (a non-GAAP financial measure) of 26.6% for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with 18.2% for the same period a year ago.
Drivers included Equity net revenues of $6.3 billion (figure and period correct; the brief omits that this was a record and up 69% from a year ago)

**Wealth Management:** Reported net revenues of $8.9 billion for the second and quarterly ended June 30, 2026, compared with $7.8 billion a year ago. (net revenue figure correct; the 30.5% pre-tax margin is not stated anywhere in the brief)

The segment added $148 billion in net new assets for the quarter. (figure, period and basis correct; the brief omits that this was a record and that just over half came from IPO-related inflows of Workplace clients)
The Board of Directors declared a $1.15 quarterly dividend per share, an increase of 15 cents, payable on August 14, 2026.
The Board of Directors reauthorized a multi-year common equity share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, without a set expiration date, beginning in the third quarter of 2026.
The Standardized Approach CET1 capital ratio was 14.8% as of July 15, 2026. (current-period figure correct; the 15.0% prior-year comparison is omitted)
